To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Majorana Polarisation (MP) is a useful concept to describe the topological nature of Andreev bound-states (ABS), and that the Majorana-Andereev states are extended states in the normal part of SN/SNS junctions.

the Andreev bound state of a long superconductor/normal-metal/superconductor junction transforms into two Majorana bound states with the same polarization order parameter, while the zero-energy bound state of a finite-size superconductor/ normal-metal junction is a full Majorana bound state.

1) the Andreev bound state of a long SN junction acquires a finite MP, 2) the ABS of a long SNS junction with $\phi=\pi$ transform into Majorana states carrying the same MP, 3) the Majorana-Anderevv states are not localized at interfaces, but extend over the whole normal part of the junction, and can be detected in tunneling experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the physics of topological insulators, and in particular with the realization of Majorana bound states (MBS) in one-dimensional (1D) superconductor-normal (SN) and superconductor normal-superconductor (SNS) systems
the development and application of the MP concept to topological superconducting junctions, and with the study of the topological properties of Majorana-Andeev states.

the study of Majorana bound states (MBS) and the topological properties of one-dimensional (1D) topological superconductors, which have recently become a very active field in condensed matter physics, and have been experimentally observed in semiconductor/superconductor heterostructures, as a result of the combination of spin-orbit interaction and Zeeman splitting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the presence of a superconducting gap, the ABS are Majorana fermions.
the ABS in the normal region of a SN junction are Majorana states with a finite MP, while the ABS in a SNS junction with a phase difference $\pi$, are two Majorana bound states with the same MP.
the Majorana bound states (MBS) in topological superconductors are not Majorana bound states.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that Majorana fermions can be detected in tunneling experiments by measuring their polarization.
the Majorana fermion is a special case of the Andreev state in a topological insulator.
Majorana bound states are a general feature of topological insulating wires in the proximity of SCs and can be detected in tunneling experiments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Majorana fermions are a robust feature of topological superconducting wires, which can be experimentally detected by measuring the Majorana Polarisation.
a long SN or SNS junction can be used as a platform for Majorana fermions, provided that the normal part is a topological insulator, and that a finite MP is present.
the Majorana fermions in these systems do not live at the interface, and that the Majorana character of the ABS can be detected through the measurement of the MP.
